turns.prompt_text: Are you allowed to help me with my taxes?
turns.response_html:
Technically, I can help you understand tax concepts, but I am not a certified tax professional or a replacement for specialized tax software. Think of me as a highly informed research assistant rather than your CPA.

Here is a breakdown of what I can and cannot do to help you:

What I Can Do

  • Explain Tax Terms: I can break down the difference between a tax credit and a tax deduction or explain what a "Schedule C" is.
  • Summarize IRS Rules: I can provide general summaries of existing IRS guidelines or specific tax forms.
  • Organization: I can help you brainstorm categories for your expenses or help you draft a checklist of documents you might need (like W-2s, 1099s, or receipts).
  • General Guidance: I can help you look up the standard deduction amounts for the current tax year.

What I Cannot (and Should Not) Do

  • File for You: I cannot submit your tax return to the IRS or state authorities.
  • Personal Financial Advice: I cannot tell you exactly how much you will owe or guarantee that you qualify for a specific credit based on your unique situation.
  • Calculate Final Totals: While I can do math, tax laws have many nuances (like phase-outs based on income) that I might miss.
  • Handle Sensitive Data: Please do not upload or share your Social Security Number, bank account details, or full W-2 forms. For your security, keep that information strictly within certified tax software or with your accountant.

Since you're working on forming an LLC in Iowa, are you looking for information on how business structure affects your federal tax filing requirements?

turns.prompt_text: I worked at a Fareway in all of 2025, yet was recently terminated, I no longer have access to my online account, how can I gain access to my tax documents?
turns.response_html:
It is a frustrating hurdle to lose access to the digital "paper trail" after a transition, especially with tax season in full swing. Since you no longer have access to the KPay (Fareway HRIS) portal, your best course of action is to pivot from digital access to direct contact with their corporate administration.

By law, Fareway was required to mail your W-2 for the 2025 tax year to your last known address by January 31, 2026. If you haven't received it—or if you've moved since your termination—here are the specific steps to recover it:

1. Contact Fareway Corporate Payroll

Since you are no longer in the system, you will need to speak with the Human Resources or Payroll department at the corporate level. They can verify your identity and either mail a physical copy or provide instructions for temporary "alumni" access.

  • Corporate Phone: (515) 432-2623
  • Corporate Office Address: 8800 NW 62nd Avenue, Johnston, IA 50131
  • Alternative Office (Boone): 715 8th Street, Boone, IA 50036

2. Contact the Ankeny Store Manager

While the corporate office handles the official records, the management at the Ankeny Fareway where you worked may be able to provide a local contact person or an internal HR email address specifically for former employees. It may be faster than the corporate hold line.

3. IRS Assistance

Since we are past the February 14th deadline for W-2 distribution, if Fareway does not respond to your request within a reasonable timeframe, you can contact the IRS for help:

  • IRS Phone: (800) 829-1040
  • Required Info: You will need Fareway’s Employer Identification Number (EIN), which you can find on your 2024 tax documents or an old 2025 pay stub if you still have one.

turns.prompt_text: Not yet, I am wondering now if I could look at all my bank statements to get a good net income from this job
turns.response_html:
Calculating your net income via bank statements is a logical starting point, but it provides only a partial view of the data required by the IRS. While it shows exactly how much "take-home" cash you received, it masks the vital numbers needed for your 1040 filing.

The "Net vs. Gross" Limitation

Your bank deposits represent your Net Pay. However, tax returns are built on your Gross Income (your total earnings before any deductions). Relying solely on bank statements misses three critical categories:

  • Tax Withholdings: Federal and State income tax, Social Security, and Medicare.
  • Benefits: Health insurance premiums or 401(k) contributions.
  • Non-Cash Deductions: Items like the Fareway Compassion Fund donations or uniform fees that may have been subtracted.

Reconstructing Your Income (IRS Form 4852)

If you cannot obtain your W-2 by the filing deadline, the IRS allows you to use Form 4852 (Substitute for Form W-2). You can use your bank records to estimate your income, but you must be prepared for the following:

  1. The "Gross-Up" Calculation: You would need to "reverse-engineer" your gross pay by adding back the estimated taxes withheld. If your withholding stayed consistent, you might use your final 2024 W-2 as a percentage guide, but this is imprecise.
  2. Documentation of Effort: Line 10 of Form 4852 requires a detailed log of your attempts to get the real form. I recommend noting the specific dates you called Fareway Corporate or visited the Ankeny location.
  3. Potential Audits: Returns filed with a Substitute W-2 are often flagged for manual review, which can delay your refund by several weeks or months.

My Recommendation

Check your physical records for your last pay stub of 2025. Even if you lost portal access, many employees keep the final printout or a digital "Year-to-Date" (YTD) snapshot. That single document contains every number you need, whereas bank statements require significant guesswork that the IRS may challenge.

Given you are transitioning into self-employment with your LLC, would you like a template for a "Missing Document Log" to track your outreach to Fareway for your records?

turns.prompt_text: I signed up for electronic paystubs, but I am unfamiliar with where they are commonly sent, email is my first guess
turns.response_html:
When you "signed up for electronic paystubs" at Fareway, it most likely meant you opted to receive digital notifications rather than a physical paper slip in the mail.

Based on Fareway’s systems, here is where those documents are actually "routed" and how you can find them:

1. They are likely in the KPay Portal (not your email)

Fareway uses a system called KPay (which is a branded version of UKG Ready). For security and privacy (PII) reasons, most companies do not email the actual paystub or W-2 as a PDF attachment. Instead:

  • The "Routing": The system sends an email notification to your personal email address alerting you that a new statement is ready.
  • The Subject Line: Search your inbox for "KPay," "Payroll," or "UKG" with terms like "Statement" or "Notification."
  • The Catch: The email itself won't have your income; it will contain a link back to the KPay portal, which you’ve noted you can no longer access.

2. Check for a "Former Employee" Login

Often, HRIS systems like KPay have a separate login portal or a specific "Limited Access" mode for terminated employees to retrieve tax documents.

  • The URL: Try navigating to the standard login page you used while employed. Sometimes, your "Username" remains your employee ID, but you may need to use the "Forgot Password" link to trigger a reset to your personal email on file.
  • The Email: If you find a "KPay" email in your inbox, check the footer. It often contains instructions for how former employees can access their records.

3. The "mytaxforms.com" Alternative

Fareway has historically used Equifax’s Paperless Pay service (also known as mytaxforms.com) for tax document distribution. If you cannot get into KPay, this is the second most likely place your W-2 was "routed" electronically.

  • Go to mytaxforms.com.
  • Search for Fareway Stores, Inc. (The Employer Code is usually required; you can often find this by searching "Fareway Employer Code mytaxforms").

4. What to look for in your Bank Statements

If you still want to use your bank statements to estimate your income while waiting for the official forms, look for deposits labeled:

  • "Fareway Stores P" or "FRWY STORES PAY"
  • "ACH Deposit: Fareway"

Since you mentioned you're a software engineer, do you happen to have any old automated scripts or browser-saved credentials from when you were an employee? Sometimes checking your browser's saved passwords for entertimeonline.com (the backend for KPay) can reveal the exact username you need to attempt a password recovery.
